title: Drugs that block sex hormone action in breast, prostate and prostate growth
ariaLabel: Schematic of four steps of sex hormone signalling: aromatase makes oestrogen from androgens, oestrogen acts on its receptor in breast tissue, 5-alpha reductase makes dihydrotestosterone from testosterone, and androgens act on the androgen receptor. Aromatase inhibitors block the first step, tamoxifen blocks the oestrogen receptor in breast, finasteride blocks 5-alpha reductase, and antiandrogens block the androgen receptor.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

edges.label: aromatase
edges.info: Aromatase inhibitors (letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane) block conversion of androgens to oestrogen. They are used after menopause, when this is the main source of oestrogen.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: oestrogen receptor
edges.info: Tamoxifen blocks the oestrogen receptor in breast tissue (it is a partial agonist elsewhere, for example in the womb and bone). Fulvestrant blocks and degrades the receptor.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: 5-alpha reductase
edges.info: Finasteride and dutasteride block 5-alpha reductase, so less dihydrotestosterone (DHT) is made, and the prostate shrinks.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: androgen receptor
edges.info: Antiandrogens (flutamide, bicalutamide, enzalutamide) block the androgen receptor, so androgen signals do not reach the cell's DNA.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Aromatase inhibitors block oestrogen synthesis, tamoxifen blocks the oestrogen receptor in breast, 5-alpha reductase inhibitors block DHT synthesis, and antiandrogens block the androgen receptor. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: GnRH agonists and antagonists, abiraterone, oophorectomy, premenopausal use, partial agonist effects of tamoxifen and raloxifene, receptor status, adverse effects (thrombosis, endometrial effects, bone loss) and monitoring are left out. Hormone-driven growth is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
